nodes.label: Git and deploy workflow
nodes.rationale: Develop on claude/jolly-ramanujan-l0q173; Railway production deploys from it on every push (draft PR #1 is open for the branch). Commit messages explain why. After pushing, confirm the Railway deploy reached SUCCESS before testing live; prefer one validated change over speculative pushes. Update MEMORY.md in the same commit as any state change.

nodes.label: Security rules (non-negotiable)
nodes.rationale: Never read, print or commit .env, credentials.json or token.json; never put secrets or end-user phone numbers in code, commits, PR text, MEMORY.md or chat; scan the staged diff for GOCSPX/sk-ant/AC[0-9a-f]{32}/password= before every commit; the Postgres connection bypasses RLS so every query must be scoped by user_id.

nodes.label: Cue's earlier documents (pa_knowledge_chunks)
nodes.rationale: documents_agent also lists and searches Cue's n8n-era pa_knowledge_chunks read-only through the match_cue_knowledge SQL function, keyed by pa_users.id (profile['cue_user_id']); the function fails closed without filter.user_id. Not migrated, read in place.

nodes.label: Owner numbers and business data
nodes.rationale: Phones in BUSINESS_DATA_PHONES (Railway env var) may query the client's business tables (leads, products, documents) read-only via data_agent; everyone else gets only their own Cue records. Enforcement is the Postgres role sellify_reader with SELECT on exactly three tables plus an RLS policy, inside a READ ONLY transaction with a 10 s timeout and 50-row cap, not SQL parsing. Never bind parameters around model-written SQL (psycopg2 reads % as placeholders).

nodes.label: Per-user SDK sessions
nodes.rationale: Always pass an explicit session_id (new user) or resume (returning user) and blank CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, otherwise users bleed into one ambient session. The session id persists in sellify_users.profile._session_id and transcripts live under /data/claude (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) so memory survives redeploys. A failed resume retries once as a fresh session. A per-user asyncio.Lock stops a reminder turn and a user turn resuming the same session at once.

nodes.label: Personal memory profile
nodes.rationale: memory_agent saves facts to sellify_users.profile (never pa_users.profile, which n8n still writes); db.get_profile merges Cue's pa_users name/timezone/core_prompt with the facts, facts win. The profile is injected into every turn as 'What you know about the user'. Keys starting with '_' are internal, never facts. Contacts' emails are remembered as <name>_email facts. Timezone is per user.

nodes.label: Railway deployment
nodes.rationale: Service Sellifyagent deploys from branch claude/jolly-ramanujan-l0q173 on push (Dockerfile on the Playwright image; Procfile unused). Volume /data holds the shared Google token and Claude transcripts. DATABASE_URL points at Cue's Supabase (transaction pooler; the login is not a superuser, so SET ROLE needs a GRANT and RLS applies to every non-owner role). Limits 24 GB / 24 vCPU; peak observed 1.1 GB.

nodes.label: Reminder scheduler and follow-ups
nodes.rationale: _reminder_loop polls every 60 s -> db.claim_due_reminders (atomic pending->sending, SKIP LOCKED, retries stuck rows after 15 min, max 3 attempts) -> _deliver_reminder runs the agent with a [REMINDER TRIGGER] prompt -> db.finish_reminder records sent/failed/next occurrence from code, never from the model. Repeating reminders: at least every 10 min, created only after the user OKs, every message says 'Reply stop', and 'stop' is handled in app.py code.

nodes.label: Cue's Supabase shared database
nodes.rationale: Cue's n8n owns pa_users, pa_personas, pa_reminders, n8n_chat_histories, pa_knowledge_chunks. Sellify's own tables are sellify_users, sellify_notes, sellify_chat_history, sellify_reminders, sellify_documents, sellify_document_chunks, all with RLS enabled and no policies so the public REST API cannot read them; any new table must be added to _lock_tables. The DB also holds the client's unrelated leads/products/documents tables.

nodes.label: Plan for ~20 testers
nodes.rationale: Pre-test hardening: tester allowlist, first-message welcome flow, per-user daily cost to the DB, a 'disconnect Google' tool, a spend alert in the Anthropic console. User side: add each tester's Gmail as a Google test user, register a WhatsApp template for >24 h reminders. Capacity is fine at 20 concurrent users.

nodes.label: Transcript length drives cost
nodes.rationale: Each turn re-reads the whole SDK transcript; Claude's prompt cache lasts 5 minutes and WhatsApp messages arrive further apart, so a long transcript is re-written into cache on most turns. A 100k-token history costs about $0.25 per message before any work. Proposed fix: rotate sessions at ~40k tokens with a handover summary.

nodes.label: WhatsApp 24-hour window (Twilio error 63016)
nodes.rationale: Business-initiated WhatsApp messages more than 24 h after the user's last message need an approved content template or Twilio rejects them. Reminders after a quiet day therefore need a registered template (backlog).

nodes.label: Per-user Google OAuth
nodes.rationale: Each WhatsApp number connects its own Google account; tokens live in sellify_users.profile._google_tokens. Owner numbers (BUSINESS_DATA_PHONES) fall back to the shared /data/token.json. One consent covers Calendar, Gmail read/send/modify, Drive read + drive.file, Docs, Sheets, Tasks, Contacts. The consent screen is in Testing mode so every user's Gmail must be added as a test user. Stored tokens are loaded with the scopes they were granted, so older tokens keep working and has_scope() is truthful.

nodes.label: Scope check per Google tool
nodes.rationale: Every Google tool gets its client from google_auth._scoped_service, which returns None when the token lacks that service's scope; the tool then answers with scope_not_granted, i.e. the user's personal link, which adds the missing scopes on top of the earlier grant (include_granted_scopes). OAUTHLIB_RELAX_TOKEN_SCOPE=1 keeps a partial grant storable.

nodes.label: Signed personal connect link
nodes.rationale: /oauth/google/start is gated by a token nonce.exp.sig (HMAC with TEST_WEBHOOK_TOKEN, 30 min, nonce->phone map in memory; the phone never appears in the URL). A bare or tampered link returns 403, because whoever completes the flow becomes that number's Google account.

nodes.label: Drive, Docs and Sheets tools
nodes.rationale: drive_agent: search_drive_files (name + fullText, shared drives), read_drive_file (Docs/Sheets/Slides exported as text; PDF/DOCX/text via extract_text), save_last_file_to_drive; workspace tools create/append a Google Doc and create/append/read a Google Sheet. Appending is the only edit; drive.file, never full drive.

nodes.label: Google Tasks and Contacts tools
nodes.rationale: tasks_agent lists/adds/completes Google Tasks (to-dos, distinct from timed reminders). search_contacts is given to the calendar and email agents so 'call with Sarah' finds her email before anyone is asked; it also searches 'other contacts' when that scope is granted.

nodes.label: Operational autonomy and stop conditions
nodes.rationale: Build, deploy and test end-to-end without asking, except for: security risks, changes that could alter or double-write Cue's pa_* tables, Twilio routing changes, deleting Railway services/volumes/env vars or changing the Google OAuth client, sending real email/WhatsApp to other people, and browser automation that logs in or takes financial actions.

nodes.label: Truth about actions rule
nodes.rationale: Prompts keep the rule that the assistant only claims something is done if a tool returned success; prompts stay short and principle-based rather than long example lists.

nodes.label: Booking approval gate
nodes.rationale: browser_agent fills forms with Playwright; commit-looking buttons (book/confirm/reserve/submit/pay) are refused until booking_gate.is_approved(user). Only app.py sets that, by matching the user's own next message against a yes/no regex; one commit per approval, 10 min TTL. Password/card fields and login pages are refused outright. Guest bookings only; nothing persisted; screenshots served from /media/<token>.png.

nodes.label: Sellify is Cue (n8n migration)
nodes.rationale: This repo is the n8n-based Cue assistant rebuilt on Railway with the Claude Agent SDK. n8n Cue's Twilio subscription was deleted 2026-09-23; only Sellify replies. Sellify reads Cue's pa_* tables but writes only sellify_* tables because the n8n reminder scheduler still runs (writing pa_reminders would double-fire).

nodes.label: Lessons carried over from n8n Cue
nodes.norm_label: lessons carried over from n8n cue
nodes.rationale: Truth about actions (the biggest recurring bug was claiming events/reminders were created without a tool call); principles not lists (Cue's prompt shrank from 12 KB to under 5 KB); fail closed on missing identity; ambient session state is not identity.

nodes.label: Manager agent and specialist subagents
nodes.rationale: One manager (Cue) delegates to calendar, email, notes, research, documents, reminders, data, images, memory, browser, drive and tasks subagents. Each AgentDefinition restricts tools; allowed_tools at the top level must hold the union of every subagent tool name (ALL_TOOL_NAMES) or the subagent cannot call it.

nodes.label: Metered API key, not a claude.ai login
nodes.norm_label: metered api key, not a claude.ai login
nodes.rationale: A deployed third-party product must authenticate with a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; Anthropic's terms forbid offering claude.ai login or rate limits to third-party products, including Agent SDK agents.

nodes.label: Why the Claude Agent SDK
nodes.rationale: The SDK is Claude Code as a library: ClaudeAgentOptions.agents defines named subagents with their own prompt and tool allow-list and Claude delegates to them itself, so no hand-rolled supervisor loop is needed. Tools run in-process via create_sdk_mcp_server. Note: README's setup section predates per-user Google, web search via WebSearch/WebFetch and the extra subagents; MEMORY.md is the current source of truth.

nodes.label: Voice notes, photos, generated images
nodes.rationale: audio/* -> Whisper transcript prefixed [Voice note, transcribed]; image/* -> PIL downscale <=1568 px -> base64 image block via the SDK streaming-input form (the only way images reach query()); images_agent generates pictures (gpt-image-1) and charts (matplotlib) served from /media/<token>.png and attached as WhatsApp images.

nodes.label: Document upload pipeline (text only)
nodes.rationale: PDF/DOCX/text sent on WhatsApp is downloaded, text extracted, chunked (~1200 chars, 150 overlap), embedded with OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (matching Cue's Canon) and stored in sellify_documents/_chunks (pgvector). Only extracted text is stored, never the original file. Retrieval is on demand only; the user rejected auto-retrieval on every message.

nodes.label: Twilio media 404 retry
nodes.rationale: Twilio fires the webhook before the media has always landed: the first GET can 404 about 200 ms after the webhook. download_media retries 404/5xx from Twilio hosts with pauses 1/2/3/5 s; credentials go only to *.twilio.com hosts and never follow redirects to the CDN.

nodes.label: Testing approach
nodes.rationale: Syntax via python3 -m compileall; route tests with fastapi.testclient mocking Google/Twilio (DB init failing locally is expected); live agent tests via POST /webhook/test, which this sandbox can only reach through the Railway probe function; print response bodies, not just status codes.

nodes.label: WhatsApp request flow
nodes.rationale: Twilio webhook -> FastAPI returns empty TwiML at once -> background task -> PersonalAssistant.ainvoke -> claude_agent_sdk.query() with the manager prompt and subagents -> reply via Twilio REST split at 1600 chars. POST /webhook/test runs the same agent synchronously for testing.

nodes.label: Webhook security
nodes.rationale: Real Twilio signatures are verified on /whatsapp/webhook (forged -> 403); /webhook/test needs X-Test-Token and returns 404 without it. This sandbox cannot reach railway.app or api.twilio.com, so live tests run as one-off scripts on the delivery-status-check Railway Function and are read back from its logs.

nodes.label: WhatsApp typing indicator
nodes.rationale: _keep_typing calls Twilio's typing-indicator API (public beta) every 20 s during a turn with the inbound MessageSid.

nodes.label: Full email and attachment reading
nodes.rationale: read_emails returns only Gmail's ~200-char snippet, which once cut a date in half; read_email fetches the whole body (HTML -> text with comments stripped, <=12k chars) and attachment names; read_email_attachment runs a PDF/DOCX/text attachment through the same extractor as uploads; modify_email archives/labels/trashes (never permanent delete); save_email_attachment_to_drive uploads to Drive.

nodes.label: Model pinned to claude-sonnet-5
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE_MODEL env var (default claude-sonnet-5 in src/config.py) passed as ClaudeAgentOptions(model=...); subagents inherit. Chosen 2026-09-24 for cost: about 2.5x cheaper than the SDK's Opus default. Every turn logs 'Turn cost: $..., models=...' from ResultMessage.total_cost_usd.

nodes.label: Last-sent file kept 30 minutes
nodes.rationale: Documents are stored as text only and photos not at all, so src/utils/recent_files keeps the last WhatsApp file or photo per user in memory for 30 minutes (<=10 MB) purely so 'save that to my Drive' can upload the original bytes.

nodes.label: Claude Agent SDK gotchas
nodes.rationale: permission_mode='bypassPermissions' fails as root (use 'dontAsk'); dict-style @tool schemas mark every field required (use explicit JSON Schema); tool names are mcp__<server>__<tool>; Playwright's sync API cannot run on the asyncio loop (browser tools use the async API in-process; Chromium as root needs --no-sandbox).

nodes.label: New-tool convention
nodes.rationale: @tool(name, description, JSON_SCHEMA) with explicit required list, blocking I/O in asyncio.to_thread, return {'content':[{'type':'text','text':...}]}, add the name to the relevant *_TOOL_NAMES so it reaches ALL_TOOL_NAMES; per-user data bound via a closure factory; fail closed with a plain message, never fabricate.

nodes.label: Per-user tool closures
nodes.rationale: Per-user tools are built per request via closure factories such as build_notes_tools(user_phone), not via tool arguments or contextvars, because those do not survive the SDK subprocess boundary. A tool-builder signature mismatch once broke every turn after deploy, so run PersonalAssistant()._build_options(phone, profile) for an empty and a populated profile before pushing agent/tool changes.

nodes.label: Per-user isolation
nodes.rationale: All data is keyed by phone number at two levels: an explicit SDK session id per number (never the CLI's ambient session, which once attached the wrong user during testing) and tools rebuilt per message via closure factories rather than trusting the LLM to pass an internal user id.
